q-37192.problem: Given that $f(x,y)=2xy+{y}^{2},$ find $\frac{∂f}{∂\theta },$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
q-37192.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $f(x,y)$ with two independent variables $r$ and $\theta ,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂\theta } & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂\theta }+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂\theta } \\  & =-\frac{∂f}{∂x}r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\frac{∂f}{∂y}r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r$ and $\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta , \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂\theta } & =-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +(2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ) \\  & =2{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )+{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-95109.problem: Given that $w(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}),$ find $\frac{∂w}{∂r},$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
q-95109.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $w(x,y)$ with two independent variables $r$ and $\theta ,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂r} & =\frac{∂w}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂r}+\frac{∂w}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂r} \\  & =\frac{∂w}{∂x}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{∂w}{∂y}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $w$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂x}=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},\,\frac{∂w}{∂y}=\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r$ and $\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂x} & =\frac{2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }, \\ \frac{∂w}{∂y} & =\frac{2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂r} & =(\frac{2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta })\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +(\frac{2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta })\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{2r({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{2}{r}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95115.problem: Given that $h(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2},$ find $\frac{∂h}{∂r},$ where $(x,y)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta )$ are the corresponding plane polar coordinates.
q-95115.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $h(x,y)$ with two independent variables $r$ and $\theta ,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ and $y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂r} & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂r}+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂r} \\  & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{∂h}{∂y}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $h$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x}=2x,\,\frac{∂h}{∂y}=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r$ and $\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta , \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =-2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂r} & =(2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -(2r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2r({cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-95171.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $u(x,y,z)$ with three independent variables $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and $z=z,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =\frac{∂u}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂z}+\frac{∂u}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂z}+\frac{∂u}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂u}{∂z}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $u$ with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂z}=2{x}^{2}z+xy\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =2{r}^{2}z{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={r}^{2}(2z{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Given that u(x,y,z)=x2z2+x2y2+xyz, find ∂u∂z, where (x,y,z) are Cartesian coordinates and (r,θ,z) are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.

a
2r2(zcos2⁡θ+sin⁡2θ)
b
cos⁡2θ+r2zsin⁡2θ
c
r2(2zcos⁡2θ+12sin2⁡θ)

2zcos2⁡θ+12sin⁡2θ
e
r2(2zcos2⁡θ+12sin⁡2θ)

Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function u(x,y,z) with three independent variables r,θ, and z, where x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ, and z=z, we have

∂u∂z=∂u∂x⋅∂x∂z+∂u∂y⋅∂y∂z+∂u∂z⋅∂z∂z=∂u∂z.

First, we find the partial derivatives of u with respect to z:

∂u∂z=2x2z+xy

Writing the above results in terms of r,θ, and z, we get

∂u∂z=2r2zcos2⁡θ+r2cos⁡θsin⁡θ=r2(2zcos2⁡θ+12sin⁡2θ).

q-95174.problem: Given that $h(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+4{x}^{2}{z}^{2},$ find $\frac{∂h}{∂z},$ where $(x,y,z)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.
q-95174.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $h(x,y,z)$ with three independent variables $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and $z=z,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂z} & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂z}+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂z}+\frac{∂h}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂h}{∂z}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $h$ with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂z}=8{x}^{2}z\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂z} & =8{r}^{2}z{cos}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
